    - Ah. The one who carried my question. Have you found an answer yet? No? Good. Neither has he.
    - My lanterns hang on the high landings now, I hear. Ordinary ones. Do you know what an ordinary lantern of mine is worth? Ruan does, now.
    - The wood you brought is drying in the back. Do you still want to know why? Good. Keep wanting.
    - Questions, is it? I like questions. What is yours?
        - *Choice:* Who are you?
        - *Choice:* How do your lanterns work?
        - *Choice:* Your apprentice?
        - *Choice:* Goodbye.
    - Who am I? Who does the market say I am? Gunna, then. Master lantern-maker. The craft came down from the Magicians of the first camp, one pupil at a time, and never written down.
    - My great-aunt Seona taught me at ten, when my hands were small enough for the finest work. A hand lantern takes me days. A quay lantern, most of a month. Why would anyone want it faster?
    - How does the tide know when to turn? Some things you learn with your hands, *Player*, and some you never learn at all.
    - Tarran. Half his lanterns are brilliant and half do not light, and I have never had a pupil whose good half was so good.
    - Is he the one for the rest of it? I have not decided. It is not his hands I am unsure of. Tell me, what do you think a lantern is for?
    - Go carefully. Mind the dark corners.
